claims.text: In-situ TEM can elucidate mechanistic aspects of oxidation in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
XPS can elucidate mechanistic aspects of oxidation in Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3.
In-situ TEM can reveal elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates in the alloy during oxidation.
XPS can reveal elemental redistribution associated with nanoprecipitates in the alloy during oxidation.
The initial alloy state is additively manufactured and contains dual nanoprecipitation.
Elemental redistribution and oxidation reactions involving the nanoprecipitates govern or contribute to oxidation behavior.
In-situ TEM or XPS analysis will improve understanding of oxidation behavior and material degradation.
Cast and wrought counterparts have lower strength than the additively manufactured alloy.
The extent of oxidation degradation may vary with oxidation conditions.
The extent of elemental redistribution may vary with oxidation conditions.
The proposed analysis is expected to reveal significant elemental redistribution or oxidation reactions.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis concerns whether the techniques can elucidate oxidation behavior, but the falsification rule treats an observed absence of significant redistribution or oxidation reactions as failure. A well-resolved null result could itself elucidate the behavior and improve understanding, so it would not necessarily falsify the stated methodological hypothesis.
